name: macd_signal_momentum_v1
author: claude-4.6-opus
thesis: MACD(12,26,9) on 1-min bars generates a momentum signal when the MACD line crosses the signal line, but the key edge comes from the MACD histogram acceleration: when the histogram is not only positive but INCREASING (histogram[t] > histogram[t-1] > histogram[t-2]), momentum is accelerating and the trend is strengthening. This triple-increasing-histogram condition filters out the many false MACD crosses that plague basic implementations. The inefficiency is that most traders look at MACD line cross (binary signal) rather than histogram slope (continuous acceleration measure). Histogram acceleration captures the rate of change of momentum, which is more predictive of continuation than the momentum level itself.

long.confirmation: histogram has been accelerating for 3 consecutive bars (momentum building)

short.confirmation: histogram has been decelerating (becoming more negative) for 3 consecutive bars

entry.entry_price: market order after 3-bar histogram acceleration confirmed

exit.target: 0.4% from entry OR MACD histogram deceleration (hist_accel < 0 for longs)
exit.stop_loss: 0.25% from entry OR MACD line crosses below signal line
exit.signal_exit: exit when histogram acceleration reverses (hist[t] < hist[t-1] for longs)

filters.time_filter: no entries before 09:30 (MACD needs warmup) or after 14:45
filters.trend_filter: VWAP alignment required (long above VWAP, short below)
other_filters: skip if MACD histogram has changed sign >4 times in last 50 bars (choppy)

edge.edge_decay_risk: moderate — MACD is well-known but histogram acceleration is less commonly used as primary signal

weaknesses: MACD(12,26,9) was designed for daily bars — on 1-min bars, the lookbacks are very short (26 min) and noisy
Histogram acceleration can be caused by a single large bar, creating false acceleration signals
The 3-bar acceleration requirement means entry is delayed — by the time signal fires, much of the move may be done
prior_art: MACD by Gerald Appel (1979). Signal line crossover is standard. MACD histogram analysis is from Thomas Aspray (1986). Histogram acceleration as a distinct signal is discussed by Elder ('Trading for a Living'). The histogram divergence/acceleration concept adds value beyond basic MACD cross.
notes: Edge math: 0.48 * 40bps - 0.52 * 25bps = 19.2 - 13.0 = 6.2 bps gross. Costs ~11 bps. Net ≈ -4.8 bps. Negative on paper. The histogram acceleration filter is the key innovation — need to validate if it genuinely improves win rate vs basic MACD cross. If it pushes WR to 0.52+: 0.52*40 - 0.48*25 = 20.8 - 12 = 8.8 bps, still below costs. Needs further work.
